documents.summary: The TLC syllabus guide asks instructors to state a generative AI policy and offers three model statements. Each statement says the rule applies to that course only and that violations count as academic dishonesty.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule itself: it asks "What is your policy on how students should engage with generative AI" and offers three model statements (permitted, permitted on certain assignments, "strictly prohibited"), so it delegates with tiers.

units.why: The page asks instructors to state a policy: "What is your policy on how students should engage with generative AI". That is a syllabus-statement requirement for instructors, so P09 (an AI statement in the syllabus).
units.anchor: What is your policy on how students should engage with generative AI
units.frag_start: What is your policy on how
units.fit_note: It is phrased as a prompt among suggested syllabus topics, not a hard mandate.

units.why: The page offers three model statements headed "Usage permitted..." / "Usage not permitted", i.e. a menu of named levels; P05 fits since it names categories of permitted use, and the stance is left to the instructor.
units.anchor: Usage permitted on certain assignments with appropriate acknowledgment
units.policy: The guide offers three model syllabus statements: AI permitted in the course with acknowledgment, permitted on certain assignments with acknowledgment, and not permitted.

units.why: Model statement 1 says AI "is permitted to augment the learning experience"; this is a default-permit rule for the course, so P02 and permit.

documents.title: GP-004.02 Acceptable Use of Generative AI
documents.summary: An IT-security standard on responsible use of generative AI across UTHSC. It mostly governs what data may be entered into AI tools, plus verification, bias and disclosure advice. It has little on coursework.
documents.stance_why: AI use is allowed with conditions on data: "Generative AI can safely process publicly available information" at Level 1 but "Do not enter private or confidential data" at Levels 2 and 3, so permit with limits.

units.why: The purpose is "leveraging generative artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly and ethically across all UTHSC environments", an institution-level framework statement, so P56.
units.anchor: leveraging generative artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly and ethically across all UTHSC environments
units.frag_start: To give guidance as a foundation

units.why: The scope names who the standard binds: "members of the UTHSC community who have a need to access UTHSC IT Resources", so P61 (scope).
units.anchor: members of the UTHSC community who have a need to access UTHSC IT Resources

units.why: The definition "a branch of artificial intelligence that enables machines to create original content" fixes what generative AI means here: P61.
units.anchor: enables machines to create original content

units.why: The IP definition covers entering "proprietary or confidential information into generative AI" "without express written consent from all stakeholders"; it restricts what data goes into AI, so P50 (P52 is about licensing and ownership of outputs, a worse fit).
units.anchor: without express written consent from all stakeholders
units.policy: Entering proprietary or confidential information into generative AI, including unpublished research findings, internal university data or documents, or information protected by intellectual property rights, requires express written consent from all stakeholders.
units.fit_note: Also an intellectual-property rule (consent for IP inputs).

units.why: "Researchers must consider the nature and sensitivity of scholarly data before using generative AI to support research" governs AI use in research, so P62.
units.anchor: Researchers must consider the nature and sensitivity of scholarly data before using generative AI

units.why: Data Owners must "Review and categorize data and information collected by their area of responsibility", an assignment of duties to a named role, so P80.
units.anchor: Review and categorize data and information collected by their area of responsibility
units.fit_note: Role duty is data classification, a prerequisite for AI data rules.

units.why: "The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is responsible for providing strategy and direction" for security standards and compliance; it names who owns and enforces the policy, so P80.
units.anchor: The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is responsible for providing strategy and direction

units.why: "Researchers cannot put data that are confidential, contain sensitive information, or are subject to specific legal or ethical requirements ... into any generative AI" without anonymization and consent, so a data-protection ban: P50.
units.anchor: Researchers cannot put data that are confidential, contain sensitive information

units.why: "Users of UTHSC IT Resources are responsible for complying with this Standard" puts the duty to follow the policy on users; the nearest type is P77 (comply with policy).
units.anchor: Users of UTHSC IT Resources are responsible for complying with this Standard.

units.why: "must adhere to the University of Tennessee System Administration (UTSA) acceptable use policy and UTHSC acceptable use standard" says AI use must follow existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: must adhere to the University of Tennessee System Administration (UTSA) acceptable use policy

units.why: "Users should assume that all consumer generative AI products make data publicly available" warns about data exposure, so P50.
units.anchor: assume that all consumer generative AI products make data publicly available

units.why: "all data that has not been explicitly classified is considered Level 3 or high-risk data by default" sets a default data-handling rule that decides what may be entered into AI: P50.
units.anchor: has not been explicitly classified is considered Level 3 or high-risk data by default
units.frag_start: All UTHSC data need to be

units.why: For Level 1 data, "Generative AI can safely process publicly available information, general academic concepts, and non-sensitive data", a permission with conditions: P50 (data protection) is the nearest group.
units.anchor: Generative AI can safely process publicly available information, general academic concepts
units.fit_note: States a permission for low-risk data rather than a protection.

units.why: "Do not enter private or confidential data, including ... PII ... FERPA, HIPAA ... into any generative AI product" is a direct ban on sensitive inputs: P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter private or confidential data

units.why: "once data is entered, neither the individual who entered it nor the institution can directly remove it" is a factual warning behind the data rules: P50.
units.anchor: neither the individual who entered it nor the institution can directly remove it

units.why: "be cautious of claims by product providers" about products being "AI"-enhanced; no existing type covers skepticism of vendor claims (P65 is institutional vendor review, P31 is output verification), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: be cautious of claims by product providers
units.uncovered_note: Users should be skeptical of vendor claims that a product uses AI or performs better.

units.why: "Think critically. Evaluate and corroborate information obtained from generative AI tools" tells users to verify AI output: P31.
units.anchor: Evaluate and corroborate information obtained from generative AI tools

units.why: Users should "review the requirements of the publisher/reviewer/recipient ... regarding disclosure requirements"; this points to disclosure but does not itself mandate it, so P24 with a fit note.
units.anchor: review the requirements of the publisher/reviewer/recipient of the finished product
units.fit_note: Tells users to check the recipient's disclosure rules instead of requiring disclosure itself.

units.why: "Stay informed. Follow conversations around AI technology and further updates and guidance from the university" is a duty to keep up with guidance: P102.
units.anchor: Follow conversations around AI technology and further updates and guidance from the university

units.why: "Users should independently verify the information provided by generative AI" because it "may generate responses that are not always accurate": P31.
units.anchor: Users should independently verify the information provided by generative AI

units.why: "Generative AI can inadvertently reflect biases present in the training data" names bias as a risk: P53.
units.anchor: Generative AI can inadvertently reflect biases present in the training data

units.why: Notes that AI "may produce or respond to content that is offensive, inappropriate, or violates ethical standards", a harm statement: P53.
units.anchor: may produce or respond to content that is offensive, inappropriate, or violates ethical standards

units.why: "if certain populations are underrepresented in the data used to train AI algorithms, results may be skewed" names algorithmic bias: P53.
units.anchor: certain populations are underrepresented in the data used to train AI algorithms

units.why: The header gives "Next Review: 10/26/2025", a scheduled review date: P54 (revisit regularly). The date has passed per the collect notes.
units.anchor: Next Review: 10/26/2025

units.why: "Resp. Office: Office of CyberSecurity" names the office responsible for the standard: P80.
units.anchor: Resp. Office: Office of CyberSecurity

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools
documents.summary: The College of Graduate Health Sciences policy makes instructors decide AI use in courses and research advisors with committees decide it for theses. Misuse falls under the Honor Code.
documents.stance_why: The policy states "The ultimate decision for the use of AI tools in a course lies with the instructor(s)" and gives theses to advisors and committees, so it sets no stance itself and delegates.

units.why: The purpose says the policy "addresses the use (or lack thereof) of AI tools such as ChatGTP in courses, thesis, and dissertations", setting scope: P61.
units.anchor: addresses the use (or lack thereof) of AI tools such as ChatGTP in courses, thesis

units.why: "Additional guidance may be forthcoming as these technologies evolve" says the policy will be updated: P54.
units.anchor: Additional guidance may be forthcoming as these technologies evolve.

units.why: "Irresponsible or impermissible use ... will be considered a violation of the Honor Code and adjudicated by the Honor Council" classes misuse as misconduct: P36.
